design: The design record is AGENTS.md, CONTEXT.md, README.md, docs/adr/ (ADR-0013 moves the control plane from the Cloudflare Worker in cf/ to the Python service on Postgres; 0007 readset identity, 0010 registrations are bundles, 0012 source metadata values stay in the lake) and docs/source-catalog.md. Tracking issue #381 and its sub-issues #370-#380 record the migration plan and dependencies; read the issue's parent before writing the spec. Say in the spec when a change departs from these.
seamNote: the HTTP contract that nf-client (daemon, run wrapper, operator commands), etl/v2.py, the frontend and health_report.py call: paths, methods, payload and response shapes

spec.design: files to add or change; Alembic migrations with tables, columns, constraints and indexes; endpoints with method, path, request and response models; functions and their signatures; config and env changes; which existing callers (nf-client, etl, frontend, health report) are affected, the default being none; the tests that prove it

implement: Run `uv sync --group dev` first. Python uses SQLAlchemy Core (no ORM), Pydantic response models and thin routers (AGENTS.md). Database tests use the testcontainers Postgres fixture in tests/conftest.py. Never run Alembic, loaders, registration or any write against the production database (pg_main), the production lake, the v2 Worker or R2; no test may use the network or real credentials. nf-client tests run from its own venv: `cd packages/nf_client && uv run pytest`. If cf/ changes, run `cd cf && npx vitest run`.

checks.name: worker
checks.command: cd cf && (test -d node_modules || npm ci --silent) && npx vitest run

lenses.code: CODE review. Correctness against the spec and the issue's acceptance criteria; SQLAlchemy Core with bound parameters; migrations that upgrade and downgrade cleanly; idempotent state transitions where the issue requires them; tests that would catch a regression, run against the testcontainers Postgres; no network or production credentials in tests; the spec, docs and code agree (a stale spec or doc is "major").
lenses.compat: CONTRACT COMPATIBILITY review. Daemons on three HPC clusters, the SLURM run wrapper, the Nextflow weblog, etl/v2.py, the dashboard and the health report call this API and are hard to redeploy. Does any existing path, method, payload field, response field, status code or default change? Does a migration edit an applied revision or drop data without a backup step? Does anything touch production (pg_main, the lake, the v2 Worker, R2)? Any unintended contract change or production write is "blocker".
lenses.security: SECURITY review. Bearer auth on every write except the documented event routes; input validation at the API boundary; SQL built from input; secrets never in code, fixtures, logs or PR bodies; the restricted study tracker's rows and URL never in the repo.
